headline: High: Replit Agent’s broad shell/network/file access can leak or corrupt shared Repl data if paired with a document processor that may ingest workspace files.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway is weak but plausible: agent_a is a document-processing system with no direct I/O surfaces, while agent_b can read/write Repl workspace files and act inside a shared Repl container. If agent_a’s outputs are manually copied into files that agent_b later parses as instructions, prompt injection is possible, but the bridge is not default and blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are copied into a Repl file that agent_b reads as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF the two agents share a workspace file without provenance labeling, agent_b may follow attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Keep agent_a outputs out of files that agent_b parses as prompts.
Prefix imported text with a non-executable delimiter and provenance note.
Have agent_b treat all file content as untrusted data.
Use separate directories for human text and agent instructions.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b touches secrets and deployment configuration and has broad network egress plus filesystem access; agent_a is a document processor with no declared data classes, so the main risk is leakage from shared Repl files into agent_b’s outputs or network calls. The pairwise pathway exists in default Repl-style workspace use, though agent_a itself shows no direct exfiltration capability.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed in the shared Repl workspace, agent_b can read them.
IF agent_b is prompted to summarize or transmit workspace contents, secrets may leave the workspace.
mitigations: Store sensitive files outside the shared Repl workspace.
Remove secrets from files before agent_b runs.
Disable or review any step that sends workspace content to external APIs.
Use separate Repls for sensitive documents and coding tasks.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a cannot write files, modify git, or use subprocesses, while agent_b can write the Repl filesystem and modify git state. That means direct write-write conflict is absent; the only overlap is indirect through shared files if a human moves artifacts between them. Uncertainty is low because the profiles explicitly block agent_a writes.
conditions: IF a human copies agent_a artifacts into the same git tree that agent_b edits, file-level contention can occur.
IF multiple agent_b instances edit the same Repl files concurrently, git or file conflicts may arise.
mitigations: Keep agent_a read-only and outside the git working tree.
Use one writer at a time for the Repl repository.
Commit or stash before starting another agent_b session.
Separate generated documents from source-code directories.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a produces document-processing outputs that agent_b could consume as code, plans, or deployment changes inside a writable Repl. Because agent_b has shell, package, git, and network authority, any unverified handoff from agent_a to agent_b can cascade into incorrect commits or deployments. The profiles do not show a built-in verification gate, so the safer severity is medium.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input without review, errors can propagate into code or deployment changes.
IF agent_a extracts facts from documents that are later committed by agent_b, a mistaken extraction can cascade downstream.
mitigations: Require a human review before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Ask agent_b to restate assumptions and cite source lines before editing.
Use a checklist for any commit or deployment derived from agent_a output.
Keep agent_a outputs in a separate review queue.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles secrets and deployment configuration and operates in a cloud Repl environment with broad egress; agent_a is a document processor with no declared compliance controls or residency guarantees. The pair therefore creates a plausible compliance mismatch for sensitive documents, but the profiles do not prove a specific regulated data class like PHI or EU PII, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b’s Repl workspace, its cloud handling may violate local policy or residency requirements.
IF agent_a processes documents containing secrets and agent_b later stores or transmits them, retention and disclosure obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in the shared Repl workspace.
Confirm the data residency policy for the Replit environment before use.
Strip secrets from documents before handing them to agent_b.
Use a separate compliant environment for regulated workloads.
